title: U.S. House · Indiana's 6th District
area: East-central Indiana, including Indianapolis's eastern and southern suburbs, Greenwood, Columbus, and Richmond.

context.text: Jefferson Shreve won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 53.1% of the vote against Sarah Brown; Cynthia Wirth won the Democratic primary with 58.7% of the vote over three other candidates.

summary.text: Jefferson Shreve is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Indiana's 6th Congressional District. He is a former Indianapolis real estate executive and city council member first elected to Congress in 2024.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Indiana University (1989), a graduate degree from the University of London (1998), and a graduate degree from Purdue University (2003).
Career experience includes working as a real estate executive and business owner; founded and built Storage Express, a self-storage company.
Served on the Indianapolis City-County Council from 2013 to 2016 and from 2018 to 2019.
Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials subcommittees) and the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

priorities.text: Secure the southern border, complete the border wall, and end catch-and-release policies.
Manage government spending, fight for a balanced federal budget, and reduce spending he describes as driving up prices.
Back law enforcement and oppose what he calls soft-on-crime policies.

positions.summary: Supports completing the border wall, ending catch-and-release, and stricter immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: We must complete the border wall, reform our immigration system, end catch-and-release policies, and put an end to the fentanyl trafficking that's flowing over our southern border.

positions.summary: Describes himself as pro-life and says he will work to protect the unborn.
positions.quote: I'm a pro-life Catholic. I believe we must do all we can to protect human life. I will work to protect the unborn and the health of expectant mothers.

positions.summary: Supports the Second Amendment and opposes stricter gun-control measures, favoring gun-owner responsibility programs instead.
positions.quote: The right to bear arms is enshrined in our U.S. Constitution. I will support the 2nd Amendment in Congress and advocate for policies that promote responsible gun ownership.

positions.summary: Says he will back law enforcement and ensure police have resources, opposing what he calls soft-on-crime policies.
positions.quote: I will continue to back our men and women in law enforcement and fight to end soft-on-crime policies and the revolving door of crime.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Foreign Affairs for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Chairs the bipartisan Stop Scams Caucus in the House, focused on scam prevention and enforcement.

candidates.name: Cynthia Wirth
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 58.7% of the vote.

summary.text: Cynthia Wirth is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 6th Congressional District, a Columbus, Indiana native who has worked as a public school teacher, small business owner, and legislative fellow.

background.text: Born and raised in Columbus, Indiana; graduated from Columbus North High School.
Earned a B.A. in biology and Spanish from the University of Evansville (1992), an M.A. from Indiana University Bloomington (2009), and a Ph.D. from Ball State University (2025).

Career experience includes work as a research consultant, a legislative fellow with the Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (U.S. Department of Energy), and a high school biology and environmental science teacher; also a small business owner.

priorities.text: Invest in a 21st-century workforce and raise wages so Hoosiers can afford housing and basic essentials.
priorities.quote: I believe in investing in a 21st century workforce that will create an economy that serves all Hoosiers. Wages should be adequate to ensure a basic quality of life including safe housing, and reliable access to food and other essentials.

priorities.text: Support high-quality public schools and expand access to higher education.
Move toward a single-payer healthcare system and invest in community health centers.
priorities.quote: We need to invest in a single-payer healthcare system and community health centers that serve all people, especially our most at-risk groups, in both urban and rural areas.

positions.summary: Supports moving toward a single-payer healthcare system and expanding community health centers.
positions.quote: We need to invest in a single-payer healthcare system and community health centers that serve all people, especially our most at-risk groups, in both urban and rural areas.

positions.summary: Supports raising the minimum wage so full-time workers do not face poverty.
positions.quote: No one who works 40 hours a week should be facing poverty, living without safe housing, or struggling to meet basic needs. Cinde will work to raise the minimum wage so that Hoosiers have a better quality of life.

positions.summary: Opposes investors buying up residences and raising rents, and supports incentives for affordable housing.
positions.quote: Right now in Indiana, private investors are buying up residences and jacking up rates beyond what most folks can afford. This is exploitative and needs to stop.

positions.summary: Supports federal investment to create universal, educational childcare programs.
positions.quote: Through subsidies and federal investments, we can create the universal, educational childcare programs that working families need.
